html:
The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is a union of West African countries set up by the Treaty of Lagos in May 1975. Its aim was to build a common market and bring the region's economies closer.

Fifteen states signed, led by Nigeria under Yakubu Gowon and Togo. Cape Verde joined in 1977. A 1979 protocol promised free movement of people, so citizens of member states could travel and live in each other's countries, although Nigeria's mass expulsion of migrants in "Ghana Must Go" in 1983 showed its limits.

From 1990 ECOWAS took on a military role. Its force, ECOMOG, led by Nigeria, intervened in the civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone. Later the community pushed back against coups by suspending members and imposing sanctions.

In 2024 the military governments of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger announced they were leaving, to form their own Alliance of Sahel States, and their exit took effect in 2025. ECOWAS now has twelve members and has its headquarters in Abuja.
sum: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is a union of West African countries set up by the Treaty of Lagos in May 1975. Its aim was to build a common market and bring the region's economies closer.
